findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, so they can answer "what is it" and "why does it matter" before scrolling.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: Someone visiting Athena's home URL gets a page titled after a different project, firstmate. Nearly all of the page is about firstmate's internals, so the newcomer has to work out from the second paragraph that this is a sample of Athena's output, not documentation for Athena.
findings.source: title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The page shows off a different ability (reading and explaining a project) from the main one it describes (making a traced commit). A newcomer never sees what an Athena commit, cost record or verdict looks like.
findings.source: lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it" vs. "turns a short request into a change to a code repository"

findings.text: The page links to its next steps from the top. The Next steps section is concrete: the repo link, the clone command, the prerequisites (git 2.40+, a C linker, curl, Claude Code or npm), ./setup.sh, and a sample command, athena ask "add a changelog". The "what to do next" question is fully answered.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The page says Athena is written in Rust but does not list a Rust toolchain as a prerequisite or say whether setup.sh installs one. A newcomer can't tell whether to install Rust first.
findings.source: lede: "written in Rust"; Next steps: "have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm"

findings.text: This link is aimed at the repository owner but sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step. A first-time reader may think they have decisions waiting.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision"

findings.text: The "Start here" section begins with seven firstmate-specific terms before saying what firstmate does. That is heavy going for a newcomer, though each term is defined plainly and traced to a claim.
findings.source: Start here, "Words used first": captain, yolo, in scope, green, red, local-only landing, home

findings.text: Every statement links to claims, which link to file lines at a pinned commit, and the page says openly that nothing was run. This backs up the promise of traceability the lede makes.
findings.source: Claims and sources: links such as "bin/fm-spawn.sh:194-197" with a "read" mark; Limits of this study f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read"

findings.text: This section points to a studies/ folder without a link or saying which repository it lives in, so a newcomer can't follow it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
